findings: The current public ingress contract is synchronous; aiogram is asynchronous and requires an event-loop/session bridge.
Aiogram would replace Telegram object parsing and HTTP but not Eva's person binding, group consent, durable ingress or ambiguity-safe delivery ledger.
Aiogram's default HTTP session does not retain Eva's explicit one-megabyte provider-receipt limit without additional custom transport code.
The dependency also forces a core Pydantic upgrade, widening this change beyond Telegram.
The current connector and application boundary passed 12 focused tests unchanged.
reopenWhen: Telegram media, webhooks, callback queries or rich message editing enter the product route.
Eva's ingress boundary becomes async-native without a compatibility bridge.
A candidate removes the durable provider layer while preserving response limits and receipts.
nonClaims: This does not claim the custom connector is generally better than aiogram.
This does not approve permanent custom Telegram protocol growth.
No live service, token, database, route or container was changed.
